symbols.name: number of axes
symbols.meaning: The number of axes of an array, which counts its dimensions.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes of an array, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, and let $S=\prod_i s_i$ be the number of positions in the array.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The length of axis i of the array, which counts the positions along that axis.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes of an array, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, and let $S=\prod_i s_i$ be the number of positions in the array.

symbols.name: array size
symbols.meaning: The number of positions in the array, which is the product of the axis lengths s_i.
symbols.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes of an array, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, and let $S=\prod_i s_i$ be the number of positions in the array.

symbols.name: normalized transform
symbols.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform applied along every axis of the array, normalized by 1/S.
symbols.quote: The theorem takes its transforms by the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_s$, applied along every axis and normalized by $1/S$.

relations.quote: The theorem takes its transforms by the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_s$, applied along every axis and normalized by $1/S$.
The theorem concerns the [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) $u*v$, taken along every axis, so each index wraps around modulo its axis length.
